name: Cap des Trois Fourches
hero_subtitle: A dramatic Mediterranean peninsula — cliffs, empty coast and one of northern Morocco’s wildest headlands.

overview.title: Wild edge of the Rif coast
overview.p1: Cap des Trois Fourches is a long, sparsely built peninsula of cliffs and open Mediterranean light — a different world from the lagoon city.
overview.p2: Come for scenery and the feeling of space, not for services. Roads can be slow; start early and carry water and food.
overview.p3: It is one of the strongest nature days you can take from Nador when weather and road conditions cooperate.

food.title: Food near Cap des Trois Fourches
food.p1: Services on the peninsula are limited — pack a full picnic and water, then eat a proper meal back in Nador or at a coastal stop on the return.
food.li1: Bring sandwiches, fruit and extra water.
food.li2: Do not count on restaurants at every viewpoint.
food.li3: A late seafood dinner on the corniche works after the drive back.
food.li4: Stock up in town before leaving Nador.
food.li5: If a roadside café is open, confirm prices first.
food.p2: Self-sufficient packing is the rule for a full Cap day.

q1.question: How far from Nador?
q1.answer: A meaningful road trip — plan half or full day, not a quick hop.

q2.question: Can I swim?
q2.answer: Possible in places when calm; this is open coast, not a supervised city beach.

q4.question: Best season?
q4.answer: Spring and autumn for comfort and clear views.

q5.question: Do I need a 4x4?
q5.answer: Depends on how far you push; many visitors use a normal car with careful driving and local advice.
